Get the turns of a sitting in order

Source: R/query-views.R
get_sitting_timeline.Rd

Reads the v_sitting_timeline view: one row per action (turn), in document order. The view is joined to sittings for the date and chamber and, when include_text = TRUE, to actions for the text.

Usage

get_sitting_timeline(
  sitting_id = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  include_text = TRUE,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

sitting_id

Filter on sitting_id: a vector of values or matches_pattern().

date

Sitting date: a Date or "YYYY-MM-DD" string, a vector of them, or in_range() (a year bound covers the whole year).

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

include_text

If TRUE (the default), add the content column. Results with content are held to the lower size ceiling, getOption("ausparl.max_rows_text").

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per action, ordered by sitting_id then seq, with columns sitting_id, date, chamber, seq, action_id, debate_title, subdebate_title, action_type, PHID, speaker_name, and content when include_text = TRUE. Zero rows if nothing matches. With collect = FALSE, an unordered lazy table with the same columns.

Details

A collected result is ordered by sitting_id and then seq, the action's position in the sitting, and limit keeps the first rows in that order. The lazy table (collect = FALSE) is unordered, so it can be aggregated in DuckDB (for example with dplyr::count()); add dplyr::arrange(sitting_id, seq) if you need the order. speaker_name is the member's current members.DisplayName, not their name at the time, and is NA where the action has no PHID. Stored values are returned unchanged, and no turn-type filter is applied.

See also

get_interjections(), get_sittings()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
get_sitting_timeline(sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15", include_text = FALSE)
#> # A tibble: 151 × 10
#>    sitting_id    date       chamber   seq action_id debate_title subdebate_title
#>    <chr>         <date>     <chr>   <int> <chr>     <chr>        <chr>          
#>  1 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       1 house_20… N/A          N/A            
#>  2 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       2 house_20… MINISTERIAL… N/A            
#>  3 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       3 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  4 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       4 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  5 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       5 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  6 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       6 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  7 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       7 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  8 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       8 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#>  9 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house       9 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#> 10 house_2002-1… 2002-10-15 house      10 house_20… QUESTIONS W… Indonesia: Ter…
#> # ℹ 141 more rows
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: action_type <chr>, PHID <chr>, speaker_name <chr>
get_sitting_timeline(date = in_range("2019-01-01", "2019-12-31"), limit = 5)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 11
#>   sitting_id     date       chamber   seq action_id debate_title subdebate_title
#>   <chr>          <date>     <chr>   <int> <chr>     <chr>        <chr>          
#> 1 senate_2019-1… 2019-11-26 senate      1 senate_2… N/A          N/A            
#> 2 senate_2019-1… 2019-11-26 senate      2 senate_2… N/A          N/A            
#> 3 senate_2019-1… 2019-11-26 senate      3 senate_2… DOCUMENTS    N/A            
#> 4 senate_2019-1… 2019-11-26 senate      4 senate_2… DOCUMENTS    N/A            
#> 5 senate_2019-1… 2019-11-26 senate      5 senate_2… DOCUMENTS    N/A            
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: action_type <chr>, PHID <chr>, speaker_name <chr>,
#> #   content <chr>
db_disconnect()
